description:
The Rabbi explains how “there are very good alternatives” to a solution between Palestine and Israel that don’t involve the Palestinian Authority.

A Foreign Office spokesman said: “We condemn this practice in the strongest possible terms. Payments to terrorists and their families are unacceptable and undermine the pursuit of peace and stability in the region.

“The Palestinian Authority have made clear the practice has ended. We welcome the steps taken to prove this, including by auditing the payments they make to families. We call on them to publish the results and to take action should there continue to be concerns.”

Officials said the British Government had “consistently” raised the issue of the “pay for slay” policy with the PA, adding that they had “taken positive steps” to wind down the practice, which included promising to audit any payments made with UK funding.

The PA declined to comment.

description:
The former prime minister Sir Tony Blair speaks to The Sunday Times about British politics, the opportunities and risks of artificial intelligence, and the conditions under which he would consider Britain rejoining the European Union.

He also discusses President Trump’s influence on defence spending among Nato allies, his role in developing a plan for Gaza’s future and how the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan changed his views on building democratic institutions.

00:00 – Inside the Tony Blair Institute
00:43 – Why Britain’s political debate feels stuck in the past
02:21 – AI is like fire: the opportunities and risks for government
04:36 – The structural flaws holding back Western democracies
07:00 – The strict conditions for Britain rejoining a reformed EU
10:29 – Has Donald Trump been a net positive or negative for Nato?
12:15 – Inside negotiations for a new governance plan in Gaza
